newsitem.title: USA: Outback says Q1 earnings below expectations.
newsitem.headline: Outback says Q1 earnings below expectations.

text.p: Outback Steakhouse Inc said Thursday it expects earnings for the quarter ending March 31 to fall short of analysts' expectations of $0.40 to $0.41 per share by ten to twelve percent.
The shortfall, said the company, can be attributed to soft sales in February and to date in March in the Outback Steakhouse concept.

Comparable store sales were down 3.2 percent in February (4.8 percent before adjusting for leap year in 1996) and are running between three and four percent lower in March after being up 3.1 percent in January.

The company said results have also been impacted by a two percent decline in per-person averages and soft sales throughout the state of Florida. An unusally mild winter in the North this year kept levels of tourists and other vacationers to the Sunshine State below usual seasonal levels, the company said.

The company attributed the decline in per person averages to the recent addition of entree salads, hamburgers and sandwiches to the dinner menu, which the company said has resulted in lower customer expenditures.

The company also said that while a television advertising for its Carrabba's units has not contributed to the profitability of the company in the first quarter, it is encouraged by the results in the advertising campaign and expect a more positive result.
